comments.author: CodapopKSP
comments.body:
I'm thrilled to release my latest passion project, Microcosm, an evolution simulator that uses mutation and natural selection to achieve diverse speciation from a single common ancestor. Art and animations made by Claude Opus 5.5, sound design by me (the old fashioned way, with a microphone and a DAW), and concept designed and tuned over the course of many weeks.

This is definitely less of a game and more of a "fish tank in a box with ASMR" kind of vibe, but there's also a Field Notebook for players to log their observed species in. It starts off slow and then produces fresh, interesting visuals and species for tens of hours.

Apologies for the warnings on Windows and Mac, since I'm not a signed publisher and I'm not gonna pay Microsoft or Apple hundreds of dollars just to be one for a free game.

[https://codapop.itch.io/microcosm](https://codapop.itch.io/microcosm)

replies.author: StarsSpawn
replies.body:
I played this hours  on the default seed and cell genes yesterday, it was pretty cool.

Sadly the common ancestor cells perished in around 8 years (not sure if it's accurate because apparently 1 year = 2 days in game) and I could do nothing but watch them die, but i don't remember seeing a text saying their species went extinct.

I created too many upwellings and couldn't cancel them which made the events cover my entire screen, also built a wall but couldn't remove it afterwards. Wish we could cancel them when we want. Or even place them where we want 

Love the game though and I thought it was so fun to watch them evolve and find their own ways to survive, after I launched a meteor some cells had no way to live but to go down and consume dead matter and minerals of their cousins.

A few things I'd like to see: more player interferance with the cells. Sometimes just watching them isn't enough. What if the player can control the cell, by dragging them around to safety or food for example? The player doesn't want to see their species go extinct after all the hours of gameplay so he will interfere. Other ways would be that the player can sprinkle things into the water or air. For example, food or toxins. I noticed that toxins weren't really seen in the game although there are settings to view them, along with others like nutrients, etc. The events the player can launch are a bit limited, only 4 when we have 10 number keys on a keyboard.

That's all I had to say, nice work on your game and I will definitely play it again (today!)

replies.author: CodapopKSP
replies.body:
I'm so happy to hear that! I actually took your suggestions and worked them into v0.6.0, so feel free to go download it! It includes a new "Acts of God" button on the right side that gives a few tools for manipulating the environment, plus 4 new calamities/events. You can also cancel events by clicking an "x" on the event indicator on the top left. Funny enough, most of these tools already existed in order to get shots for the trailer, but I had them hidden.

These new features do make it feel like more of a game rather than just a very resource-intensive desktop background. However, species aren't meant to survive long term, since they will all eventually be replaced by offspring who are better adapted to their environment. You can think of the species itself evolving and continuing on in a new form rather than going extinct (in terms of its lineage stopping).

This will be even more apparent when I add in sexual reproduction, though I still have to work out a few design questions and also do extensive tuning.

This release also includes significant documentation. It might be a bit much for casual players, but it's there in case you want to read how any of it works. The complex math in the doc shows just how much time went into tuning the model to get interesting results.

Anyway, thanks for playing, and I hope the game brought you lots of joy!

replies.author: StarsSpawn
replies.body:
That's great! Thanks to replying to my incredibly long comment, I can't wait to explore what acts of god and other features the update has. Looking forward to it!

it's very true that the game is resource extensive, I've yet to get a fast forward speed higher than 8x but maybe it's because my pc is lower end lol. 

You said most species aren't supposed to last so long, yet one of my favorite species has survived for 20+ years and it's ancestor species that looked very similar to it lived for around 10 years. Once they got down to only one member of their species yet they did not die out. They will regularly reach low numbers (50 members or below) and skyrocket when there is food available to 500+. I've tried activating the plague but it wouldn't hit them or would hit other species. I've also tried shooting meteors but the meteor lands randomly, and after a year they flourish once again as spring and summer arrives.

replies.author: CodapopKSP
replies.body:
Oh that's interesting! In my experience they usually only last a few years, maybe 10 at most. But there are definitely times where their evolved ancestors are vary similar.

The plague (when triggered manually in old versions or now when it happens randomly) affects the organism with the highest population count. As an Act of God it affects whichever organism you click.

Fast-forward speeds are definitely tied to CPU capability. My desktop (older) sometimes can't get above 2-3x though can get up to 7-12x if populations are lower. My M4 Mac can stay above 12x fairly often. It's just a matter of how many genomes and other calculations it has to track and is one reason why eyes and antennas don't have a cone-shaped range (calcs were too expensive). I am not sure it can get much more performant though since I already did a ton of optimization.

replies.author: StarsSpawn
replies.body: Thanks for the update, with the acts of god panel I killed that predator species by lowering the sea level lol. Also killed all the photosynthesizing organisms though, so I had to recultivate them. I tried the plague out and it's cool to see which members can survive through evolving so they aren't affected. One thing I noticed is that if there are tens of thousands of organisms, the game lags less and fast forward is still faster than if we killed all of those organisms.
